column1: # Citations for cadence rules with no locator, in the 10 most populous states (CA, TX, FL, NY, PA, IL, OH, GA, NC, MI): FL, PA, OH, and NC have none uncited. One row per rule; the shape of election_cadence (government_kind, function, name_pattern, period_years, phase, locator, source url). # Columns: table (CALENDAR or special-district-elections), state, government_kind, function, name_pattern, period_years, phase, statute (locator), url, note.

60 ILCS 1/50-5 (township officers elected at the regular township election for 4-year terms); 10 ILCS 5/2A-1.1
column10: consolidated election is April of odd years

column8: MCL 168.642c (a school district shall hold its regular election for the office of school board member at the general November election); MCL 380.384
column10: read on the legislature site 2026-11-12; the general November election is the November regular election date of MCL 168.641, so the rule covers all districts, not only community districts

column8: MCL 168.358 (general November election in each even-numbered year for township officers); Const. 1963 art. VII § 18
column10: terms are four years per Michigan Townships Association

column8: N.Y. Town Law § 80 (biennial town election each November of even years from 2025; town justices excepted); N.Y. Election Law § 15-104 (village election third Tuesday in March unless the village chose another date)
column10: the Even Year Election Law was litigated; see https://nytowns.org/Towns/Towns/Announcements/Even-Year-Election-Law-Update.aspx. Villages: https://newyork.public.law/laws/n.y._election_law_section_15-104

column8: N.Y. Town Law § 175 (fire district annual election on the second Tuesday in December)
column10: covers fire districts only; school districts are in election_cadence.tsv (Educ. Law § 2002); town water, sewer, and lighting districts are run by the town board and elect nothing; library trustees: see the next row

column8: N.Y. Educ. Law § 260(2) (trustees of a library established by a school district are elected by the legal voters in the same manner as school board trustees); Educ. Law § 2002(1) (third Tuesday of May)
column10: applies to school-district public libraries only; city, village, and town library trustees are appointed

column8: Tex. Elec. Code § 41.001 (uniform election dates: first Saturday in May and November Tuesday after the first Monday)
column10: city terms and date choice are in Tex. Elec. Code § 41.0052 and city charters

column8: O.C.G.A. § 21-2-9(a) (county officers not elected under § 21-2-139 are elected in the November election next preceding the expiration of the term of office); commissioner terms are set by local act
column10: FindLaw text current as of 2024-03-28; (a) names county officers, not commissioners, and sets the November before term expiry, so the even-year phase rests on the local acts; the 2025-26 bill S.B. 422 changes only subsection (c), municipal elections

column8: Cal. Elec. Code § 10403 (districts consolidate with the statewide general election); each county water agency act sets its own board election
